title: How to make a copy of a document in Google Docs on Mac: browser steps
metaTitle: How to Make a Copy of a Document in Google Docs on Mac
description: Learn how to make a copy of a document in Google Docs on Mac: open File, click Make a copy, name it, pick a folder and click OK.

intro: To make a copy of a document in Google Docs on Mac, open the file, click File at the top of the page, then choose Make a copy. Type a name, pick a Drive folder and click OK, and Google creates a separate file you can edit without touching the original.
tldr: Open the document, then go to File > Make a copy. Name the copy, pick a Drive folder and click OK.
Google Docs runs in your browser, so there is no separate Docs app to install for this job.
Google's Mac shortcut list has no shortcut for Make a copy. Open the File menu with Control, Option and F.
The copy uses your Google storage, not the owner's, even when you copy a file someone shared with you.
If Make a copy is missing, the owner has probably restricted copying. Ask them to check the sharing settings.

blocks.text: What you need before you start

Google Docs does not come as an app you install on a Mac for this job. You work in a web browser, and the File menu inside the document does the copying. The steps here work in the browser you already use on your Mac. Check the requirements first, so you do not stall halfway through.

items: A Google account with access to the document.
A web browser on your Mac. Google Docs runs in the browser, not in a standalone app.
An access level that allows copying. The owner can restrict this, so check your role.
Enough free Google storage for the new copy, because a copy counts toward your quota.

blocks.text: Make a copy in Google Docs on Mac from the File menu

This is the route most people use. Open the document, then look at the menu bar inside the Google Docs page, just below the document name. Do not use the File menu at the very top of your Mac screen. That menu belongs to your browser, and it will not show Make a copy.

Click File, then Make a copy. Google opens a small dialog with a name field, a location picker and a comments option. The name field starts with Copy of followed by the original name. Change it before you click OK, so you can tell the copy apart later.

rows: Sets the file name. The default is Copy of plus the original name.
Use a name that shows this file is the copy.
Lets you pick the Drive folder for the copy.
Choose the folder before you click OK.
Option to share the copy with the same people as the original.
Read who can open the copy before you send it on.
Carries the comments and suggestions into the copy.
Leave it off for a clean draft.
Appears only when the box above is ticked. Adds resolved items.
Tick it only if you need the closed threads.
blocks.caption: Fields in the Make a copy dialog and what to check before you click OK.

blocks.text: Google's help page covers the name, location and comments options. The option to share the copy with the same people comes from Workona, a third-party guide. Your dialog may label things a little differently, so read each field before you click OK.
Make a copy from Google Drive without opening the document

Use this route when you already know which file you want. Go to drive.google.com/home in your browser and find the file in the list. Right-click the file, or click the three-dot menu on its row, then choose Make a copy. The same dialog opens with the same fields.

blocks.title: Trackpad right-click
blocks.text: On a Mac trackpad, a two-finger click opens the right-click menu. If that does nothing, hold Control and click instead. The three-dot menu works without a right-click at all.
Copy a document someone shared with you

You can copy a file that someone shared with you, if the owner allows copying for your access level. The copy belongs to you. Google's storage help says the copy uses your storage quota, not the owner's. The original still counts toward the owner's quota.
Keep an eye on your own storage when you copy large shared files. If a team makes many copies of one long report, the space adds up quickly. Check your storage in Drive before you start a batch.
Decide what happens to comments and suggestions

The option called Copy comments and suggestions surprises people. When it is on, the comments and suggestions in the original come along to the new file. When you also tick the sub-option for resolved items, the closed threads come along too. Turn the option off when you want a clean starting point.
When to keep comments and when to leave them out

items: Keep them when a reviewer is partway through and you want their notes in the new file.
Keep resolved items only when the history matters, such as a review trail you must preserve.
Leave them out for a template, a new client draft, or any file that goes to people who should not see internal notes.

blocks.text: Why Make a copy is missing or greyed out

Sometimes the option is not there. Google's help pages list no error message for this, so the cause below comes from secondary sources. The likely cause is a restriction the owner set. The owner opens the Share menu, clicks Settings, and checks the options under People who can download, copy, print, and access.

blocks.title: Not confirmed
blocks.text: Google's sharing page confirms this setting. It does not say whether the setting removes Make a copy for viewers and commenters. Third-party guides disagree on that point, so ask the owner to test it with you.

If the file sits in a shared folder, the folder's permissions take priority over the file's download settings. In that case the owner has to change the folder, not only the file. Changing the file alone will not fix it.
Keyboard shortcuts for Google Docs on Mac

Google's Mac shortcut page lists no shortcut for Make a copy. You can still keep your hands on the keyboard for most of the route. Press Control, Option and F together to open the File menu. Then use the trackpad to pick Make a copy.

items: ⌃⌥F opens the File menu in Google Docs.
⌘C copies selected text from the original.
⌘⇧V pastes without formatting, which keeps your new file clean.
⌥/ opens the tool finder, a search box for menus and tools.
⌘/ shows the full shortcut list inside Google Docs.

blocks.text: Work on the copy offline on Mac

Offline access has its own rules. Google's offline help says offline Google Docs needs Chrome or Microsoft Edge. Safari is not on that list. You turn on offline access in Drive settings, then add the Google Docs Offline extension.
Set this up while you have a stable connection, not at the airport. Then test it by turning off Wi-Fi and opening the copy. A setup you have never tested is a setup that fails at the worst moment.
Mistakes people make when they copy a Google Doc

items: Editing the original by mistake. Read the file name in the top left before you type.
Saving the copy to the wrong folder. Pick the location before you click OK, not after.
Sending old comments to a new group. Untick Copy comments and suggestions for a clean file.
Sharing the copy with the same people without checking. Read the sharing before you send the link.
Assuming every shared file can be copied. The owner decides, and folder rules can override the file.

blocks.text: Where Lazur fits in when you copy a doc

Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in the notch on your Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘, which is Option and Command together, to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where Make a copy is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it.
Lazur does not click for you. It shows you where things are, or it guides you one click at a time and waits for each click. You still choose the name, the folder and the comment setting.
Next steps after you make the copy

Rename the copy if you skipped that step, then check the folder and sharing. If you want to add a header or page numbers to the copy, the guides are ready: [how to add a header and footer in Google Docs on Mac](/how-to/add-a-header-and-footer-in-google-docs) and [how to add page numbers in Google Docs on Mac](/how-to/add-page-numbers-in-google-docs).

If you write by voice, the [voice typing guide](/how-to/use-voice-typing-in-google-docs) walks through the setup on Mac. For more on the app page, see [AI assistant for Google Docs on Mac](/apps/google-docs).

faq.question: Is there a Google Docs app for Mac that I can use to make a copy?
faq.answer: Google Docs does not come as a separate app you install on a Mac. You make the copy in your browser, either from the File menu inside the document or from the Make a copy option on the Drive page.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for Make a copy in Google Docs on Mac?
faq.answer: Google's Mac shortcut page lists no shortcut for Make a copy. Press Control, Option and F to open the File menu, then choose Make a copy with the trackpad or mouse.

faq.question: Does the copy count against my storage or the owner's storage?
faq.answer: Your storage. Google's storage help says a copy of a shared file uses your storage quota. The original still counts toward the owner's quota.

faq.question: Why can't I see Make a copy on a file someone shared with me?
faq.answer: The owner has probably restricted downloading, copying or printing for your access level. Ask them to check Share, then Settings, under People who can download, copy, print, and access. Google's help does not confirm that this removes Make a copy, so ask them to test it.

faq.question: Can I choose a different folder for the copy?
faq.answer: Yes. The dialog has a location picker. Choose the Drive folder before you click OK. You can also move the copy later from Drive.

faq.question: Will my comments and suggestions come along to the copy?
faq.answer: Only if you tick Copy comments and suggestions. Resolved items come along only when you also tick the sub-option that includes resolved comments and suggestions.

faq.question: Can I work on the copy offline in Safari on Mac?
faq.answer: Google's offline help says offline Google Docs requires Chrome or Microsoft Edge. Safari is not on that list, so use Chrome or Edge for offline work.

faq.question: Can Lazur make the copy for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate apps for you. Hold Option and Command, ask where Make a copy is, and Lazur circles it. You can also ask for a walkthrough, and Lazur guides you one click at a time.

task: Make a copy of a Google Doc on Mac
appliesTo: Google Docs in a Mac web browser, including files shared with you
requirements: A Google account with access to the document
A web browser on your Mac
An access level that allows copying, which the owner can restrict
Enough free Google storage for the new copy

steps.name: Open the document
steps.text: Open the document in your browser. You can go to docs.google.com, pick the file, or open a link someone sent you. Wait for the page to load before you go on.

steps.name: Open the File menu
steps.text: Click File at the top of the Google Docs page, under the document name. Do not use the File menu in the Mac menu bar at the top of the screen, because that menu belongs to your browser.
steps.tip: Control, Option and F opens the File menu from the keyboard.

steps.name: Choose Make a copy
steps.text: Click Make a copy in the File menu. Google opens a dialog with the name, location and comments options. Google's help page uses the same path: File, then Make a copy.

steps.name: Name the copy
steps.text: Type a name in the top field. The default is Copy of plus the original name. Pick a name that tells you what this copy is for, such as a draft for a new reader.

steps.name: Pick a location
steps.text: Use the location picker to choose a Drive folder for the copy. Choose it before you click OK. Moving the file later means one more step in Drive.

steps.name: Set comments and suggestions
steps.text: Tick or untick Copy comments and suggestions. If you tick it, you can also choose whether to include resolved items. Leave both off for a clean draft.

steps.name: Check sharing if the option appears
steps.text: If the dialog offers to share the copy with the same people, read who is listed before you continue. Check the sharing now, not after you send the link.

steps.name: Click OK
steps.text: Click OK to create the copy. Then check the file name in the top left and the folder in Drive. If the name or folder is wrong, rename or move the copy from Drive.
steps.tip: Fixing the name later is quick, but a wrong folder is easy to forget.

shortcuts.action: Open the File menu in Google Docs

troubleshooting.problem: Make a copy does not appear in the File menu
troubleshooting.fix: Check your access level first. If the owner restricted copying, ask them to change the setting under Share, then Settings. Google's help does not confirm that this removes Make a copy, so test it.
Make a new copy with Copy comments and suggestions unticked. The option only applies at the moment you make the copy, so the existing copy keeps its comments.

troubleshooting.problem: The copy landed in the wrong folder
troubleshooting.fix: Find the file by its name in Drive, then move it to the right folder. Next time, choose the location before you click OK.
Use a two-finger click on the trackpad, or hold Control and click. You can also use the three-dot menu on the file's row.

troubleshooting.problem: Offline copy will not open in Safari
troubleshooting.fix: Google's offline help requires Chrome or Microsoft Edge. Open the file in one of those browsers after you turn on offline access.
